questions.q: Why did Tara's father refuse to send his children to public school?
a: He believed public schools brainwashed children
He could not afford the school fees
He wanted them to work in the family business
He thought the schools were too far from home
questions.why: Lesson 1 says her father believed public schools brainwashed children, so the children were nominally homeschooled instead.

questions.q: What first inspired Tara to study for college?
a: Her brother Tyler's example of studying and getting in
A teacher who noticed her talent and offered help
A book about Cambridge that she found in town
Her mother's encouragement to leave the farm
questions.why: Lesson 1 says her older brother Tyler studied and got into college, and his example planted the seeds for Tara.

questions.q: What surprised Tara about her first visit to a doctor?
a: It was not the horrible place she had been taught
The doctor refused to treat her without insurance
The visit was far more painful than expected
The medicine made her sick for several days
questions.why: Lesson 2 says she went to a doctor for the first time at college and was surprised it was not a horrible place.

questions.q: How did Tara's father try to pull her back at Harvard?
a: He demanded she accept a blessing or be seen as a threat
He offered to pay her tuition if she returned home
He wrote to the university asking them to expel her
He threatened to cut off contact with her siblings
questions.why: Lesson 3 says her father insisted she accept a blessing to cast out Satan, or she would be treated as a threat to the family.

questions.q: Where did Tara eventually earn her doctorate?
a: Cambridge University
Brigham Young University
Harvard University
Oxford University
questions.why: The overview and Lesson 3 explain that Tara earned a doctorate from Cambridge University.
